question: R1
caption: Beam model and TCP geometry. (a) Normalized radial profiles of the scalar LG01 donut (fwhm = 300 nm, Balzarotti Eq. S17), the LG donut with the curvature of the vectorial zero (fwhm = 327.14 nm) and the vectorial Richards-Wolf vortex donut with circular polarization of the correct hand (lambda = 640 nm, NA = 1.4, n = 1.518, filling 5/3); dotted lines mark the ring radii (LG 300: 180.2 nm; vectorial: 192.3 nm, peak-to-peak diameter 384.67 nm). (b) I/rho^2 near the zero on a log radius axis: all zeros are quadratic, and the curvature-matched LG agrees with the vectorial profile to within 1 % for rho <= 100 nm. (c) TCP: three donut zeros (x) on a circle of diameter L (dashed; L = 100 nm shown for visibility) plus a central exposure (+); the map is the intensity of exposure 0.

question: R1
caption: Vectorial donut. (a-c) Focal-plane intensity, normalized to the ring maximum, for circular polarization of the correct hand, of the opposite hand, and for linear (x) polarization. (d) Profiles through the zero: the zero depth I(0)/I_max is 0 for the correct hand, 0.845 for the opposite hand and 0.372 for linear polarization. (e) Centre CRB (r -> 0 limit, N = 100, no background) of the TCP vs L; all vectorial beams are evaluated exactly (no interpolation grid). (f) Relative CRB difference with respect to the LG donut with fwhm = 300 nm: the curvature-matched LG (fwhm = 327.14 nm) reproduces the vectorial CRB to within 0.4 % for L <= 150 nm.

question: R2
caption: CRB maps and the discontinuity at the TCP centre (fwhm = 300 nm, N = 100). (a-d) CRB over the field of view |x|, |y| <= L for L = 50 and 100 nm, without background and with SBR = 10 (log colour scale, contours in nm; pixels on a perfect zero take the r -> 0 limit). (e) Cuts through the centre along x and y for L = 50 nm: without background the r -> 0 limit (1.605 nm) lies below the point value at r = 0 of Balzarotti Eq. S27 (1.802 nm), which excludes the central exposure with p = 0; with SBR = 10 the CRB is continuous (Eq. S31, 1.960 nm). (f) Ratio of the limit to the point value vs L, closed form (lines) and numerical Fisher computation (circles); it tends to 2/sqrt(5) only for a quadratic zero (L << fwhm).

question: R2
caption: Scaling of the centre CRB and comparison with camera localization. (a) CRB vs L (N = 100, no background): r -> 0 limit (numerical and closed form) and Eq. S27 point value; the log-log slope fitted over L = 5-40 nm (shaded, L << fwhm) is 1.004. With a perfect zero the CRB increases monotonically only for L < 360 nm (ring diameter fwhm/sqrt(ln2)), diverges there and decreases beyond (dotted). (b) CRB vs N for L = 50 nm: slope -1/2 for the limit, Eq. S27 and Eq. S31 with SBR = 10. (c) CRB vs SBR (L = 50 nm, N = 100): for finite SBR the point value equals the limit (Eq. S31) and tends to the S27 point value, not to the background-free limit, as SBR -> infinity. (d) MINFLUX (L = 50 nm) vs an ideal camera (sigma_PSF = 100 nm): continuum limit sigma_PSF/sqrt(N) and a 9 x 9 window of 100 nm pixels, without background and with SBR_c = 500 defined per pixel (total SBR = 500/81); triangles mark the photons needed for 5 nm (camera 400 and 591; MINFLUX 10.3 with the r -> 0 limit, 13.0 with the S27 point value, 15.4 with SBR = 10).

question: R3
caption: Position estimators vs the CRB (TCP with L = 50 nm, N = 100, fwhm = 300 nm, seed 42). (a) Bias along x and (b) sigma/CRB vs the true emitter position x0 on the x axis, from the centre to x0 = L (inside and outside the TCP circle, shaded: inside), for the MLE, the LMS (Balzarotti Eqs. S49-S50) and the modified LMS (Eq. S51) with SBR = 10, evaluated on the same counts (10^4 repetitions per point; the MLE searches a disk of radius 2L = 100 nm). Inside the TCP at x0 = 10-20 nm the MLE shows a bump, sigma/CRB of about 1.5 at N = 100, caused by an outlier tail; its height depends on the search-disk radius (2L here), and it disappears at N = 1000. (c) Background-free MLE at the TCP centre (search disk of radius L): sigma divided by the r -> 0 CRB limit (about 0.84, superefficient) and by the Eq. S27 point value (about 0.75) vs N, a consequence of the non-regular model (p_centre ~ r^2); the background-free LMS has sigma equal to the S27 value (1.123 times the limit). (d) Background-free MLE, N = 100: bias along x vs x0 near the centre (4 x 10^4 repetitions per point); the bias points toward the centre and is about -0.34 nm at r = (2, 0) nm.

question: R4
caption: Iterative MINFLUX vs camera localization (4 iterations, TCP diameter reduced geometrically from L = 150 to 25 nm, equal photon split, re-centring on the previous estimate, MLE, no background, 10^4 emitters per photon budget, bootstrap standard errors). (a) Final precision sigma vs total photon budget N_total (250-8000), compared with the ideal camera sigma_PSF/sqrt(N) (sigma_PSF = 100 nm), with the log-log fit for N_total >= 500 (slope -0.515, which excludes -1/2) and with the centre CRB if all photons were spent at L = 25 nm; at N_total = 1000 the variants with SBR = 10 (square) and with the adaptive L schedule (diamond) are shown. The grey cross, labelled, is the run without re-centring: its ~8 nm is an artefact of the truncated MLE search disk, not physics. (b) Ratio sigma/sigma_camera vs N_total: it falls from 0.183 at N_total = 250 to 0.158 and flattens. (c) sigma after each iteration vs the TCP diameter L_k at N_total = 1000 (250 photons per iteration), without background and with SBR = 10, together with the centre CRB of each iteration.

question: R5
caption: Finite depth of the donut zero (LG donut, fwhm = 300 nm, Gaussian pedestal of relative height eps, TCP centre, N = 100, no background). (a) Centre CRB vs L for eps = 0 (r -> 0 limit, dashed) and eps = 0.002, 0.01, 0.05, 0.15; stars mark the optimal L of each eps. With eps = 0 the CRB grows monotonically with L only for L < 360 nm (the ring diameter fwhm/sqrt(ln 2)), where it diverges. (b) L_opt/(fwhm sqrt(eps)) vs eps: the rule L_opt ~ 0.78 fwhm sqrt(eps) holds only for eps <~ 0.01 (shaded) and the ratio falls to 0.70 at eps = 0.15. (c) eps = 0.002, L = 100 nm: CRB (nm) vs distance from the centre along three directions; the minimum lies off the centre. The vertical line marks the transition scale sqrt(eps/(e a)) = 4.9 nm (a = 4 ln 2/fwhm^2), a scale and not the position of the minimum.

question: R5
caption: TCP misalignment: naive vs honest MLE (L = 100 nm, N = 500, SBR = 10; each of the four zeros displaced by delta in an independent random direction; 400 random patterns x 200 repetitions, seed 42; true positions at the centre, filled symbols, and at (L/4, 0), open symbols). (a) Mean |bias| vs delta of the naive MLE (assumes the ideal TCP) and of the honest MLE (knows the displaced zeros), with the Monte Carlo noise floor of an unbiased estimator (grey). The dotted line is 0.76 delta, a weighted fit through the origin of the naive centre values over the 7 plotted deltas (including delta = 15 nm). The principal slope quoted in the text is the noise-free population estimate (MLE on expected counts, 4000 patterns): about 0.78 at the centre and 0.85 at (L/4, 0) over delta = 2-10 nm, with |bias|/delta growing with delta. At the centre the honest MLE stays at the noise floor; at (L/4, 0) it lies slightly above it for delta >= 10 nm. (b) sigma vs delta with the honest CRB: the naive sigma changes little, so its loss of accuracy is bias; the honest sigma follows the honest CRB at the centre and lies 1-2.4 % above it at (L/4, 0) for delta <= 10 nm. (c) rmse vs delta. Error bars are the between-pattern standard errors.
